title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Plan International Ireland SQRIBE programme is implemented in Guinea. The intended outcome is that Vulnerable and Marginalised Children Realise their Rights to Access and Benefit from a Safe, Quality, Resilient and Inclusion-Based Education (SQRIBE). The objective of the grant is to meet urgent education and protection needs for children, with a specific focus on adolescent girls, out-of-school children, and children living with a disability. The programme applies a gender-transformative approach, promoting inclusive, safe, and gender-responsive learning environments that tackle harmful social norms and barriers to girls’ education. The programme also integrates comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) to equip adolescents with the knowledge and skills to make informed decisions about their health, relationships, and well-being. Key activities include financial and technical support to schools and vocational centres, community sensitisation and mobilisation in relation to child rights, particularly girls’ rights and the rights of children living with a disability, and capacity building for education stakeholders. While the programme’s overarching goal is to increase access to quality, inclusive education, gender equality is a principal objective. The intervention explicitly targets adolescent girls, the most excluded demographic from accessing education, and applies gender-transformative approaches to tackle the root causes of gender disparities in education. Activities go beyond access, focusing on shifting harmful norms, strengthening protection, and ensuring learning environments are safe, inclusive, and responsive to girls' needs. Without addressing these barriers, the education objective cannot be achieved, making gender equality central, not secondary, to the programme’s success. Inclusion and empowerment of persons with disabilities is also marked as 2 in the LTD projects because it is an equally significant objective, with targeted interventions and results demonstrating a strong commitment to ensuring the full participation and empowerment of children with disabilities within the education system.
